transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-19
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Title: POC scoping — model shortlist & benchmarks (Polestar Diagnostics)
Attendees: Jesse Huang (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Polestar Head of ML), Tom O'Neil (CTO), Priya Kapoor (Lead Data Engineer)

Summary (auto): initial scoping call to select open models for clinical lab report extraction; focus on multilingual support and tradeoffs for latency vs. cost. Agreed on 4-week POC with clear bench pass/fail.

Topics discussed: success criteria, dataset size & token mix, candidate models (Llama variants, Mistral-ish, guppy-like?), quantization, routing to Dedicated vs Hosted, security checklist.

Transcript:
00:00 Jesse (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick sound check. I see Marta, Tom, Priya — thanks for making time. Carlos from our SE team will drive the bench details.
00:22 Marta (Polestar): Hi, yeah loud and clear. Sorry we're juggling a release, so appreciate the focused agenda.
00:30 Carlos (Redwood SE): Cool, I'll keep this around the bench items. High-level: you said earlier you want both extraction of lab entities and some light summarization for patient-friendly reports, is that right?
00:45 Marta: Exactly. Two scopes — structured extraction (test name, units, abnormal flags, specimen) and then a short plain-language summary for clinicians and optionally Spanish/Portuguese translations.
01:05 Tom (CTO): Our key constraints: sub-200ms for single-record lookups in the UI is ideal, but we can accept async for bulk processing. Cost target is a big driver — we have mid-sized throughput: ~250k records/month, average report 350 tokens.
01:30 Jesse: Good — that gives us some initial sizing. Quick back-of-envelope: 250k * 350 = ~87.5M input tokens/month plus output tokens — round to 110M tokens for budgeting.
01:50 Priya: That matches our internal estimate. Token distribution is skewed — 20% very short, 60% typical 200–600 tokens, 20% long 1k+. We'll upload a token histogram.
02:10 Carlos: Perfect. On models, we're thinking open weights so you can run on-prem later. For POC we usually try 1) a base Llama2- style 13B (quantized), 2) a high-efficiency 7–8B Mistral-like candidate, and 3) a bigger instruction-tuned 33B for quality baseline. We can add a multilingual-focused model if you need that.
02:40 Marta: Multilingual is important — Spanish and Portuguese are top, French is nice to have. How do those open models behave on clinical jargon?
02:55 Carlos: Clinical domain is tricky. Off-the-shelf often gets the entities right but misses edge cases — lab-specific abbreviations. We'll run targeted prompt templates and a few-shot set. Also recommend a small in-context example bank and a lightweight fine-tune if needed later.
03:20 Tom: Fine-tune will be a later phase. For the POC we need clean metrics to decide: entity F1 target and acceptable hallucination. What do you recommend?
03:35 Jesse: From similar customers, a pass threshold is 0.90 F1 for core entities and <2% hallucination on gold test. If you want conservative, set F1 to 0.92. But depends on your tolerance — regulatory teams often want evidence.
03:55 Marta: 0.90 sounds reasonable to start. We'll flag specific entities that are must-have vs nice-to-have.
04:10 Carlos: Good. On latency: Hosted Redwood can typically hit single-request median in low-ms to sub-200ms depending on model/sequence and batching. Dedicated gets more predictable throughput. If UI needs <200ms for single record, smaller models or optimized kernels + KV caching are the path. For summarization in multiple languages, cost goes up.
04:40 Priya: What about quantization — 4-bit vs 8-bit? Does it affect hallucination or NER quality?
04:52 Carlos: Quantization often trades slight quality for big perf/cost wins. 4-bit (Q4) is a sweet spot for many; for sensitive extraction, we'd test both Q4 and Q8. Some models show minimal drop on NER; others degrade more. That's part of the bench.
05:20 Jesse: We'll include Q4 and Q8 runs in the plan. Also include a run with no quant to set an upper bound.
05:30 Tom: Data residency — a number of our EU partners require data processed in the EU. Can Redwood run POC in a VPC or region-limited mode?
05:45 Jesse: Yes. We have Hosted EU regions for evaluation; for stricter needs we can do Private (VPC) deployment or Dedicated in region. For POC benching we can run a hosted EU-backed endpoint or a private trial deployment depending on timeline.
06:05 Marta: Ok, include an EU run in the bench, at least for a sample of requests. Also SOC2 and SAML — we'll need the security pack.
06:17 Carlos: We'll attach SOC2 and the SAML/SSO integration guide.
06:20 Jesse: On the bench plan timeline, thinking: week 0 (this week) — dataset and metric finalization; week 1 — baseline runs (3 models, Q settings) on limited test set; week 2 — integration throughput runs and dedicated config; week 3 — analysis and final recommendations. That lands about 3–4 weeks. Thoughts?
06:45 Tom: That's acceptable. We have engineering capacity to integrate the test harness in week 1.
06:52 Priya: We'll need a small API contract — a simple JSON schema for input/output.
06:58 Carlos: We'll provide a sample harness that hits the model endpoints and validates the entity extraction F1. We'll also give a token logger so you can see distribution.
07:15 Marta: For metrics, define exact matching vs fuzzy matching for entities — e.g., unit variations like mg/dL vs mg per dl.
07:27 Jesse: We'll default to normalizing units and include fuzzy matching thresholds in the bench harness. We'll share the canonicalizer rules.
07:40 Speaker 1 (auto): um can you repeat the threshold for hallucination 2%?
07:45 Jesse: Yes, under 2% hallucination on the gold set as an initial target.
07:50 Carlos: On model shortlist names — we deliberately avoid exact vendor brand names in the call — but shortlist will include: 7–8B multilingual opt, 13B instruction-tuned generalist, 33B RLHF-ish baseline. We'll label them M1, M2, M3 in docs.
08:10 Priya: For multilingual, do we expect equal quality across Spanish/Portuguese? Some models are trained mostly on English.
08:22 Carlos: Often English dominates. For SP/PR (Spanish/Portuguese), pick models trained with multilingual corpora or apply few-shot examples in the native language. We'll validate with a small validation set in each language.
08:40 Marta: Regulatory-wise, we might need logs showing model versions for audit. Does Redwood provide traceability?
08:48 Jesse: Yes — model versioning, rollout history, request traces, and audit logs are available in the Console. We'll include token-level cost breakdown for the bench runs as well.
09:00 Tom: About throughput — our bulk ETL will process nightly batches of ~10k reports. We need to see throughput numbers at different batch sizes.
09:12 Carlos: We'll include throughput runs at batch sizes 1, 8, 32 and a continuous streaming run approximating your nightly load. We'll report tokens/sec and p99 latency.
09:25 Marta: Can we include an accuracy slice for hard cases — e.g., holders, ambiguous abbreviations?
09:30 Jesse: Yes add a "hard cases" holdout slice. Please flag examples when you upload samples.
09:38 Priya: On dataset — we will de-identify then upload 500 samples across the languages. We'll also attach a separate CSV with annotations for a gold set of 200 records.
09:52 Carlos: That's perfect. Bench will run against the 200 gold records for F1 and hallucination; other samples used for throughput.
10:05 Jesse: Quick note on fallbacks — if a model for some requests is too slow, we can route to a smaller model for the UI while processing the larger model async for final results. That policy is simple to set in Redwood's routing.
10:25 Tom: Good, want graceful degradation rather than full fail.
10:30 Marta: One more thing: cost targets. Can you provide estimated cost per 1M tokens for each model/quant combo so we can compare?
10:40 Carlos: We'll include cost estimates in the model shortlist doc — based on our current unit economics for Q4/Q8/no-quant.
10:48 Jesse: Ok I think we're converging. I'll send the model shortlist and cost table by EOD Wednesday (2025-05-21). Carlos will push the bench plan and the harness by Friday (2025-05-23).
10:58 Speaker 2 (auto): [crosstalk] sounds good
11:02 Marta: Great — next, who's owner on the SSO and security exchange?
11:07 Jesse: I'll own security doc exchange, but Priya will coordinate the SAML test.
11:12 Priya: Yep I'll set up a test SAML connector once we have the doc.
11:18 Tom: For the POC acceptance: we'll accept if entity F1 >= 0.90 AND p99 latency on UI paths < 500ms for the chosen model under expected load. Anything outside that goes back for tuning.
11:36 Jesse: Noted — we'll aim for median <200ms and p99 <500ms in the bench results for the UI-eligible config.
11:45 Carlos: We'll also capture memory/VRAM usage to help you plan Dedicated capacity sizing.
11:55 Marta: Thank you. Quick ask — can you include a short write-up on quantization risk and mitigation for each model?
11:59 Carlos: Yes, a one-page note per model.
12:05 Jesse: Recap of next steps (verbal): Redwood to send model shortlist + cost table, bench plan + harness, security docs. Polestar to upload samples and confirm metrics. Schedule bench kickoff 2025-05-26.
12:22 Marta: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
12:26 Jesse: Thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invites and links.
12:30 [call ends]

References/links mentioned (to be attached in follow-up):
- Benchmark harness (will be shared by Carlos)
- SOC2 report and SAML guide (by Jesse)
- Model shortlist + cost table (by Jesse)
